rules: 1 all-in crypto pick per day, 100% deployed
Spot crypto only (BTC, ETH, SOL, and other liquid coins on Robinhood)
Rotate each 6:45am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Hard stop at entry; leverage conviction, protect downside

positions.name: Ethereum
positions.catalyst: Yesterday's ETH thesis paid — the coin we held through the CPI binary was the RIGHT major and it broke out. June CPI (released Jul 14) cooled to 3.5% vs 3.8% forecast, gutting near-term Fed rate-hike odds and flipping the whole complex risk-on; ETH ran +5% and cleared the $1,800 resistance shelf it had defended all month, printing ~$1,881. The ETH-specific flow story is now CONFIRMED: U.S. spot Ether ETFs took ~$58M net inflows on the CPI day, extending the reversal that broke an eight-week outflow streak (first positive week ~$84M for the week ending Jul 11), while U.S. spot BITCOIN ETFs printed fresh OUTFLOWS led by Fidelity and BlackRock the same session — the flow arrow still points opposite directions across the two majors. Fresh ETH-forward catalyst overnight: Morgan Stanley updated its filings for proposed Ethereum (and Solana) ETFs naming Coinbase as custodian AND staking provider — the staking-ETF pipeline advancing on the record, the mechanism that converts ETH into a ~2.6-3.0% yielding asset inside a regulated wrapper (BlackRock's staked-ETH product live since Mar 12). On a confirmed risk-on tape, the correct all-in is the liquid major that owns the only improving institutional-flow story AND just confirmed a technical breakout, not the higher-beta alt chasing the same headline.
positions.driver: ETH now carries BOTH relative strength and confirmed momentum. It led the majors green THROUGH the risk-off two days ago, then led the bounce on soft CPI, closing above $1,800 for the first time this month (~$1,881 on the live feed) — a completed range breakout from the $1,700-$1,800 box that flips the old ceiling into support and gives clean structure: hold above breakout, stop below it. Runners-up rejected: BTC (~$64,668) rallied on the same CPI but its ETF complex is BLEEDING (fresh Fidelity/BlackRock outflows on the up day) — you don't go all-in on the major whose institutional bid is leaving; SOL (~$77.40) shares the MS-filing headline and would out-run ETH on pure risk-on continuation, but it is the SAME name that failed us on Jul 13 (led the bleed, not the bounce), its CLARITY-Act catalyst keeps slipping, and here the edge is 'own the confirmed flow story' so the extra beta is uncompensated; XRP (~$1.11), LINK (~$8.40), DOGE (~$0.074), AVAX (~$6.67) have no fresh idiosyncratic catalyst. Entry = dashboard canonical live feed, asOf 2026-07-15T11:53:18Z (ETH-USD $1,881.69).
positions.risks: Chasing a +5% breakout day is the core risk — ETH is now in the UPPER half of its former range, ~$80 above the $1,800 shelf, so the entry is extended and a fade back into the box (retest $1,800, then $1,731 stop) is the obvious mean-reversion. The CPI pop was partly a short-squeeze: ~$376M of crypto shorts liquidated in 24h ($127M of it ETH), and squeeze rallies routinely give back once forced buying is done. ETF inflows are real but modest ($58M) and one session old — Bitcoin's fresh ETF outflows warn that institutional appetite is uneven, and if BTC rolls over ETH will not decouple. The staking-ETF/MS-filing catalyst is a slow regulatory drip, not a next-24h event, net yield only ~2-3% after cuts. Macro remains the master variable: any hawkish Fed re-pricing, a hot data surprise, or renewed Hormuz/oil geopolitics flips the risk-on tape doing most of the work. Hard stop $1,731.15 (-8%), just under the breakout so the trade invalidates cleanly if $1,800 fails as support.
